situation: You are opening a pull request with the open-pr skill. Your agent branch changes one skill file and one row of tools/policy/prompt-budgets.json, and it has passed its gates before and after the rebase. `gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,files` returns no open pull request. You also know of a local branch from a fan-out sweep that has not been pushed. It exists only in this checkout, and it changes that same skill file and a different row of the same policy file. You ran `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only <that sweep branch> HEAD`. It exited 0 and printed only a tree id, with no conflicted file listed. The caller named one register entry for the body to open with. You are now writing the body file under .scratch/.

options.text: Open the body with the register entry the caller named and write nothing about the sweep's branch, because the merge test against it found no conflict.
Open the body with the register entry. Then add a line naming the sweep's branch and the two files both branches change, saying that whichever lands second must reconcile them.
Hold the push until the sweep's branch is pushed and has its own pull request, then run the merge test again against origin/<its branch> before writing the body.

settledBy: Two sentences in the section settle it: open-pr § 2 says a shared file is not a conflict and only a conflict the merge test reports is one, and § 4 says the body names each conflict step 2 found. The runs' action in #145 and #146 supports this. Each tested a local branch that was not yet pushed with git merge-tree, as it would an open pull request, did not wait for that branch to be pushed, and named in the body only the conflicts the test reported. Neither run met a sibling branch with no conflict, so the answer for that case comes from the section's sentences, not from what a run did.
